concepts.name: Shell and prompt
concepts.summary: Recognise the shell as a text interface that reads commands and shows output, and read the parts of a prompt.

concepts.name: Filesystem directory tree
concepts.summary: Explain that files live in a single tree rooted at / with directories nested inside, including the home directory.

concepts.name: Absolute and relative paths
concepts.summary: Distinguish paths starting at / from paths relative to the current directory, and use . and .. correctly.

concepts.name: Command structure
concepts.summary: Describe a command as a program name followed by options and arguments, such as ls -l /etc.

concepts.name: Navigation commands
concepts.summary: Use pwd, ls and cd to find where you are, list contents and move between directories.

concepts.name: Getting help
concepts.summary: Look up a command's usage with man and --help and find key facts in the output.

misconceptions.text: Linux commands and file names are not case sensitive, so File.txt and file.txt are the same file.
The cd command changes directory only for the single command that follows it.
A leading slash on a path is optional and makes no difference to where it points.

concepts.name: File and directory manipulation
concepts.summary: Create, copy, move, rename and delete files and directories with mkdir, touch, cp, mv and rm.

concepts.name: Viewing file contents
concepts.summary: Choose cat, less, head or tail to read all or part of a text file.

concepts.name: Wildcards and globbing
concepts.summary: Use *, ? and [ ] patterns so the shell expands them to matching file names.

concepts.name: Permission bits
concepts.summary: Read the read, write and execute bits for owner, group and others in ls -l output.

concepts.name: Changing permissions
concepts.summary: Use chmod with symbolic and octal modes to grant or remove access on files.

concepts.name: Redirection basics
concepts.summary: Send command output to files with > and >>, and read input from files with <.

concepts.name: Pipes
concepts.summary: Connect the output of one command to the input of another using |.

concepts.name: Searching text with grep
concepts.summary: Find lines matching a pattern in files or piped input using grep and common flags.

misconceptions.text: rm moves files to a trash folder from which they can be restored.
Using > to redirect output appends to the file rather than overwriting it.
Wildcards such as * are interpreted by each command, not by the shell.

concepts.name: Standard streams and file descriptors
concepts.summary: Redirect stdout and stderr separately or together using 2>, 2>&1 and /dev/null.

concepts.name: Text-processing filters
concepts.summary: Combine sort, uniq, cut, tr and wc in pipelines to summarise and reshape text data.

concepts.name: Shell variables and environment
concepts.summary: Set shell variables, export them to child processes, and explain how PATH resolves commands.

concepts.name: Quoting and expansion
concepts.summary: Predict how single quotes, double quotes, variable expansion and $(...) change what a command receives.

concepts.name: Script structure and execution
concepts.summary: Write a script with a shebang line, make it executable, and run it with arguments $1, $2 and $@.

concepts.name: Exit status
concepts.summary: Interpret exit codes and chain commands with && and || based on success or failure.

concepts.name: Conditionals and loops
concepts.summary: Use if, test expressions, for and while to branch and repeat in scripts.

concepts.name: Process management
concepts.summary: List processes, run jobs in the background, and stop them with kill and signals.

misconceptions.text: Single and double quotes behave identically in the shell.
Redirecting with > also captures error messages.
A variable set in a shell is automatically visible to every program it starts.

concepts.name: Regular expressions in tools
concepts.summary: Compose basic and extended regular expressions and judge which match a given text.

concepts.name: Stream editing with sed and awk
concepts.summary: Transform text with sed substitutions and awk field-based programs, choosing the right tool.

concepts.name: Robust find and xargs usage
concepts.summary: Select files by name, type, size or time with find and act on them safely, including names with spaces.

concepts.name: Defensive scripting options
concepts.summary: Evaluate how set -e, -u and pipefail change failure handling and decide when to use them.

concepts.name: Functions and argument handling
concepts.summary: Structure scripts with functions, local variables and option parsing for reusable tools.

concepts.name: Special permissions and ownership
concepts.summary: Analyse setuid, setgid, sticky bit, umask and chown effects on shared file access.

concepts.name: Scheduling and automation
concepts.summary: Schedule recurring tasks with cron, accounting for its minimal environment and logging.

misconceptions.text: Shell globs and regular expressions use the same syntax, so * means the same in both.
Piping find output into xargs is always safe regardless of file names.
set -e makes a script stop on every possible error in every context.

concepts.name: Script security hardening
concepts.summary: Assess scripts for injection, unsafe temp files, unquoted expansion and privilege risks, and fix them.

concepts.name: Advanced shell features
concepts.summary: Judge when to use process substitution, here documents, arrays and traps for cleanup.

concepts.name: Pipeline performance design
concepts.summary: Evaluate pipeline designs for speed and memory, avoiding needless processes and large intermediate files.

concepts.name: Portable shell scripting
concepts.summary: Distinguish POSIX sh from Bash-specific features and decide what portability a script requires.

concepts.name: Command-line tool design
concepts.summary: Design composable tools with clear interfaces, stdin and stdout use, exit codes and usage text.

concepts.name: Automation framework creation
concepts.summary: Create tested, logged and idempotent automation that combines scripts, scheduling and error reporting.

concepts.name: Diagnosing with system tools
concepts.summary: Diagnose misbehaving processes and scripts using tools such as strace, lsof, top and journal logs.

misconceptions.text: A script that works in Bash will work in any shell that runs it.
Quoting variables is only a style choice and never affects security.
Shell pipelines are always the best choice for any data processing task regardless of scale.
